elements.title: William Plumer Jacobs (Wikipedia — did you know?)

elements.title: Tarif-i Husain Shahi (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the illustrated manuscript Tarif-i Husain Shahi contains a rare depiction of a queen in Islamic art?

elements.title: a bulldog from New Zealand (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a bulldog from New Zealand was trained to locate wounded soldiers on the battlefields of the Western Front in World War I and guide them back to safety?

elements.title: the first biography (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the first biography of the first Japanese woman to earn a college degree was written by her great-granddaughter, who also studied abroad in the U.S.?

elements.title: Raul Meza Jr. (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the serial killer Raul Meza Jr., when asked if he was apologetic, replied: "What's the use if a person will not accept it?"

elements.title: 1930 NCAA basketball championship round game (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that after a retabulation showed an overtime was needed, Ateneo put its 1930 NCAA basketball championship round game against UST under protest as one of the two referees already left?

elements.title: Robert Yelverton Tyrrell (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Robert Yelverton Tyrrell became a professor of classics despite spending only six weeks at secondary school?

elements.title: Aquilegia gracillima (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the limited study of the Afghani plants Aquilegia gracillima, A. maimanica, and A. microcentra has been blamed on political circumstances?

elements.title: Price Tower (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Price Tower was sold for $10 in 2023?
